A larger home may be affordable on one income if the complete housing payment and other household expenses fit the income you expect after the baby arrives. Review financing and your own budget using that changed income, rather than the earnings you receive today.

A larger house is not automatically a better fit. Consider where feeding and sleep routines could happen, where a stroller can be stored, how laundry works, and whether stairs or the route from parking to the front door would make an ordinary day harder. A flexible room can sometimes be more valuable than extra square footage that is difficult to use.

A lender can help you understand financing options and a possible approval range, but you decide what payment feels sustainable for your household. Build your search around that comfort level.

A reverse mortgage is a loan that allows eligible homeowners to borrow against home equity while generally postponing repayment until a qualifying event such as a sale or permanent move. It is not free income, and the homeowner still has obligations such as taxes, insurance, and property upkeep.

Beyond general cost of living, it's worth researching how a prospective state taxes retirement income specifically, Social Security, pension income, and retirement account withdrawals are taxed very differently from state to state, and this can matter as much or more than overall cost of living for some retirees' actual financial picture.

Beyond general credentials, looking for an agent with specific experience helping relocating buyers, someone comfortable with video walkthroughs, detailed neighborhood breakdowns, and remote communication, tends to serve out of state buyers better than an agent primarily used to working with local, in person clients.

Beyond life insurance, Social Security survivor benefits, a pension's survivor option if the deceased spouse had one, or veterans' benefits if applicable can meaningfully supplement household income, and it's worth reviewing all potential benefit sources before assuming the mortgage is unaffordable on remaining income alone.

Beyond loan qualification, it's worth stress testing the actual monthly budget on one income specifically, not just what a lender approves, factoring in reduced income, any new childcare related savings from a parent staying home, and other adjusted expenses.

Beyond simple convenience, reducing physically demanding yard work becomes increasingly relevant as a long term consideration for aging in place comfortably, not just a lifestyle preference in the near term.

Beyond square footage, signs include a lack of separate space for remote work and family life, a kitchen too small to function during regular meal prep with kids underfoot, or a single bathroom creating morning bottlenecks for a family of four or more.

Beyond the mortgage itself, a single income now typically needs to cover costs previously split, property taxes, insurance, maintenance, and possibly childcare if custody arrangements require it, all factors worth including in a realistic affordability assessment.

Beyond the physical timing, aligning a move with an employed parent's available time off, rather than trying to handle a move around a full work schedule on top of a pregnancy or newborn, often matters as much as the trimester timing itself in determining how manageable the process actually feels.

Beyond the pure numbers, the psychological value of being debt free in retirement matters genuinely to many people, and a mathematically "optimal" choice to keep a low rate mortgage and invest instead isn't automatically the right choice if it creates ongoing stress about carrying debt into retirement.

Selling a home

Selling a home brings together practical decisions and personal change. Dominique helps you organize the details, understand your options, and shape a plan around your property, priorities, and timing.

Selling a large home can be worthwhile for a two person household when the replacement improves daily use, upkeep, and overall expenses. A large house can still be a good fit if its rooms and responsibilities serve the way you actually live.

Selling a larger home and buying a smaller one converts the price difference directly into accessible cash or investments, one of the most straightforward ways to use home equity for retirement funding without taking on new debt.

Selling and renting can reduce some maintenance responsibilities and provide more flexibility, but rent and lease conditions can change. Compare the full ongoing expenses and the use of your sale proceeds before giving up home ownership.

Selling avoids any ongoing landlord responsibilities and typically provides a larger, one time influx of equity compared to the slower, ongoing income from renting rooms, appealing to those who prioritize simplicity over supplemental income.

Selling before buying eliminates the risk of carrying two mortgage payments simultaneously and provides a clear number for exactly how much is available for the next purchase, though it may mean a period of renting or staying with family in between.

Selling before the divorce is final removes the home from the pool of assets still being negotiated, which can simplify and speed up the overall settlement process, and allows both spouses to move on financially with a clean division of the proceeds.

Selling does not have to be the automatic next step after losing a spouse. First check the mortgage, available income, property costs, and any estate or loan deadlines. Selling earlier may reduce carrying costs and create a known amount of cash, but the proceeds may need to be held or distributed under an agreement. Selling first can make the available purchase funds clearer, but it may require temporary housing while you find the next home. Buying first can provide continuity when financing and reserves support the overlap, so compare both timelines with a lender.

Selling first gives a clearer amount of available cash but may create a gap between homes. Buying first can reduce moving pressure but may require qualifying while carrying both properties. A coordinated closing can work, although one delay may affect both transactions. Review contingency, bridge financing, and temporary housing options before committing to a sequence.

Selling in the San Fernando Valley is property specific. Pricing, preparation, replacement home inventory, financing, and the timing of competing listings can affect whether it makes sense to move now, wait, or coordinate a purchase with the sale.

Selling may also release equity, but moving costs, taxes, repairs and the price of the replacement home affect how much flexibility you actually gain. This decision is often emotional because the property may hold years of family history.

Selling provides immediate access to the equity, which can be invested elsewhere, used to pay down other debt, or split among multiple heirs cleanly without ongoing shared management responsibilities.

Selling tends to make sense when neither spouse can afford the home individually, when neither wants to keep it, or when a clean financial break outweighs the complexity of a buyout or extended co ownership arrangement.

Selling to rent converts home equity into liquid assets that can be invested or spent down over time, a choice that trades the potential for continued home value appreciation for immediate liquidity and flexibility, a trade off some retirees value more than others depending on their broader financial picture.
